(2) Momentum exhaustion exits for biotech momentum plays — close when the signal degrades, not at a fixed price target, to allow positions to run. (3) Fixed mean reversion targets for tech positions — the thesis has a defined endpoint (recovery to pre-selloff level), close when reached. (4) Stop-losses calibrated to strategy volatility, not portfolio drawdown limit — the strategy-level stop should trigger well before portfolio-level circuit breakers are relevant.

portfolio_scope.ambition_description: Focused two-regime pipeline, not a comprehensive multi-strategy system. User is deploying $75K into a clearly defined mandate built around two areas of identified edge and opportunity. He is not trying to build an all-weather automated trading system — he is trying to systematize two specific plays he either understands deeply (biotech FDA catalyst) or has identified and manually validated (large-cap tech mean reversion). The Builder should explore deeply within these two pairs rather than generating breadth across a wide strategy space. Three to five highly validated strategies that the user understands and trusts are worth more than ten mediocre ones spanning sectors he doesn't follow.
portfolio_scope.diversification_intent: Moderate within the two defined pairs. Within biotech: diversify across catalyst sub-types (PDUFA, Phase 3, adcom) to avoid all strategies depending on the same FDA approval month. Within tech mean reversion: diversify across different trigger magnitudes and holding periods. Across the two pairs: the pairs are structurally uncorrelated by design (FDA approval momentum vs. post-earnings price recovery are different market dynamics). User does not want forced diversification into sectors or strategy types outside his mandate — authentic diversification within the mandate is preferred over superficial breadth outside it.
portfolio_scope.correlation_intent: Inter-strategy correlation should be low within each pair and very low across pairs. The mandate is explicitly designed to be uncorrelated to SPY — strategies that have high SPY correlation defeat the purpose of the Aegis allocation. Within biotech: strategies should not all be triggered by the same catalyst type in the same month (e.g., avoid a scenario where all 3-4 biotech strategies depend on a strong FDA approval month). Within tech: strategies should not all require the same market condition (e.g., all depending on a tech selloff quarter).

Biotech catalyst plays should be largely idiosyncratic — FDA outcomes are not meaningfully correlated to broad market direction. Large-cap tech mean reversion plays will have some SPY correlation by nature — this is acceptable but should be weighted as the minority of the portfolio (35% capital weight) and noted in performance reporting.
